prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve / detailed painted game sprite movement sheet.
Asset: exactly FOUR full-body rolling keys of ONE robot, in a strict 2 columns x 2 rows layout, on a 1536x1536 transparent RGBA square canvas. Read top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right. Each equal square cell is a complete cutout with generous clear alpha margins on every side. This is a travel cycle, not a character design variation or work sequence.
Reference image 1 is the chosen detailed FRONT-RIGHT movement sheet. Repaint the SAME robot and four wheel phases from a new physical side. Use its anatomy, materials and proportions, NOT its camera orientation. Reference image 2 is only the game's elevated camera. Do not horizontally flip any reference. Reference image 2 supplies ONLY the game's elevated orthographic character-camera angle, not its humanoid anatomy or gait.
CAMERA: fixed orthographic, looking down about 31 degrees, three-quarter diagonal view, 45-degree ground heading. Show tops of cap/body/wheels clearly, as this will be seen in an isometric game from above. No vanishing point, lens perspective, head-on view or low eye-level toy photograph. Same camera, scale and silhouette in all four cells.
MOTION: four restrained rolling keys. Main wheel hubs have one unobtrusive brass index/spoke progressing through quarter-turn phases 12, 3, 6, 9 o'clock in order. Tyres stay circular in 3D projection with consistent axles, width and tread. Both main wheel axles remain fixed relative to the body. Wheel contact baseline is the same within every cell. Body stays almost stable, only 1–2 pixels of suspension settle and a tiny tool/arm response; it does not hop, stride, stretch or change proportions. Preserve all parts and hand grips across keys. No new action, prop, open panel or change of design between frames.
STYLE: high-detail painted game art, warm dark-brown clean outer outlines, fine painterly surface shading, readable cream enamel and deep muted teal, restrained brass with soft wear at handled edges, black rubber tread, amber light. Coherent screw heads, seams, rim thickness and joints with actual connections. Detail should survive downsampling rather than becoming random engravings. Soft warm light from upper left, restrained edge highlights, no ground shadow or floor.
FRAMING: all four robots fully visible, including cap finial, pole lantern if present, wheels and any rear caster. Never cut a silhouette at a cell boundary. Consistent apparent size in all cells; leave at least 8% clear alpha around each robot. No scenery, text, grid, labels, platform, pedestal or background. Actual transparent background, no painted paper/checkerboard or colored rectangle. Do not include other robots or people.
TENDER: preserve the approved low, rounded maintenance helper, a friendly compact tortoise-like cream enamel shell directly supported on a deep-teal FOUR-WHEEL rubber chassis. Four small wheels, two front and two rear on two real axles; no legs, feet or loose floating wheel. One large round brass-rimmed amber spark-face with two warm oval eyes on the FRONT ONLY. Two short ivory folding arms with brass shoulder pivots and teal mitten hands stay tucked safely near the front corners during rolling. Rounded teal top service cap with a brass carry handle. A small tidy moss patch nestles at the REAR RIGHT shell seam, with a few tiny pale blossoms, no huge changing bouquet. Preserve fixed shell seams, screw placement, wheel tread, brass hubs and all joints across the four cells. Gently worn, maintained and cute, not a scarred combat machine. No working valve or extra prop in this travel sheet.
ANATOMICAL SIDE LOCK: the moss/blossom patch remains at Tender's OWN REAR-RIGHT shell seam; a small brass service coupling stays on the RIGHT flank below it. The LEFT side is plain cream enamel. Keep the same left/right arm hinges, hand shapes and front/rear hatch placement as the character turns. Do not horizontally flip the design or transfer details to the other side.
DIRECTION / ANATOMICAL VISIBILITY:
BACK-RIGHT / NORTHEAST: travel toward UPPER-RIGHT, away from the camera. Show the REAR and Tender's OWN RIGHT flank, now near. The front amber face and eyes are completely HIDDEN: a proper plain rear shell and a small rectangular service hatch with TWO VERTICAL SLITS and brass hinges occupy the rear. The moss stays on the OWN REAR-RIGHT seam, and is visibly on VIEWER-RIGHT above the near right shoulder/axle, with the small brass coupling BELOW it. Keep the left flank on viewer-left clean. The four wheels remain on the same two axles; no face or mitten painted onto the service hatch. Arms tuck around the forward corners, some parts naturally hidden from this rear camera.
Maintain the exact chosen design, camera elevation, restrained wheel motion, high detail and full-body scale in all four cells. The FOUR hub index phases should be distinguishable (up/right/down/left), not four identical keys. No new work props, valve or action.
